## How this deck works {.smaller}

This is a **living timeline** of progress on Chapter 1.

- The nightly pipeline appends a date-stamped section after midnight every day.
- Each daily section includes a short summary of what was worked on plus any new figures.
- Newest entries appear at the **bottom** — navigate forward (→) through time, backward (←) for older.

For the curated talk version, see [chapter3-slides.html](chapter1-slides.html).

# 2026-08-30 {.center}

::: {.under-review}

## What we did

- Automation-only window (08-29 → 08-30): no substantive user sessions touched Ch3.
- Corrected the authorship of the Climate Dynamics atmospheric-river reference, which had been filed under the wrong first author since 08-10, and backfilled the synthesis paragraph it never received.

## New literature

- He et al. 2026 — multi-archive SEA finds coherent post-eruption **wetting over the western United States** in PDSI, across tree-ring reconstructions, nine data-assimilation products and two model ensembles; the closest thing yet to a positive, non-coral volcanic hydroclimate signal for this region [@he2026volcaniccomparison]
- Tripp et al. 2026 — Galápagos subfossil corals record ENSO variance at ~4 ka comparable to 1959–1979 CE but *negatively* skewed, i.e. stronger cold events, against the positively skewed modern record [@tripp2026galapagos] ⚠ relevance uncertain — mid-Holocene, no volcanic analysis
- The two new references pull in opposite directions on this chapter's premise: He et al. supply a positive PDSI signal over the western US, while Wahl et al. find no clear volcanic link in California precipitation across 500 years and call it approximately white noise. Present the tension; do not resolve it yet.

:::

## 2026-04-23 — Nightly pipeline {.smaller}

**Literature:** Phase-4 AUTO block appended to `chapter3.qmd` and `literature-review.md` on ENSO–California teleconnection variability.

- Guirguis et al. (2024): ENSO modulates synoptic character of CA wet regimes but not seasonal frequency — volcanic El Niños may shift AR circulation without proportionally changing precipitation counts.
- Zamora-Reyes et al. (2022): 600-year CA hydroclimate context — recent decades show anomalously high variability driven by wet extremes.
- Evans et al. (2022): intrinsic century-scale variability in ENSO–SW-US teleconnection; motivates ensemble-based volcanic attribution.

**Bib:** 3 new entries (`guirguis2024enso`, `zamorareyes2022california`, `evans2022intrinsic`). All 24 citations resolve ✓.

## 2026-05-05 — Nightly pipeline {.smaller}

**Literature:** Phase-4 AUTO blocks appended to `chapter3.qmd` and `literature-review.md` on two-pathway volcanic hydroclimate framework.
